talk: FundBun · 2026 FinTechathon final round (29 Nov 2026, Shenzhen) · International AI Track · Topic A · 15 slides for a 15-minute pitch (about 14:10 spoken, 50 seconds in reserve) and 5 minutes of questions

slides.title: You could've gotten a Birkin.
slides.alt: Title slide. FundBun: an AI money buddy that shows you the dream you could've had, and helps you get it back. A gold Dream Mirror shows Jing's Birkin 25 (¥98,000) with a burnt Bun peeking in. 2026 FinTechathon Finalist, International AI Track, final round, 29 Nov 2026, Shenzhen. Topic A: Personal Finance Assistant. Team lead Odri Prince Sembiring (Universitas Gadjah Mada); teammate Nadine Griselda (Universitas Airlangga).
slides.notes:
[0:00 to 0:35 · 35 s] Every budgeting app tells you a number. Numbers don't hurt. Missing the thing you actually want does. FundBun is a personal-finance agent that turns your spending into the dream it costs you, and then helps you get it back, safely. I'm Odri from Universitas Gadjah Mada. My teammate Nadine from Universitas Airlangga could not travel, so I am presenting for both of us. Since the first round FundBun has grown from a phone demo into a desktop app you can restyle by chatting, and I will show that live.

Pacing: 15 slides, about 14 minutes, one minute in reserve. If the clock is tight, shorten slides 2 and 6 first.

slides.title: Overspending is invisible until it's too late.
slides.alt: The problem, in three numbers. ¥2,580 over budget is just a number: budgets speak in numbers, and numbers don't hurt. 39 studies show people neglect what a purchase displaces (opportunity cost). Alipay's Huabei bill assistant, which warns at the moment of paying, was linked to 19.6% lower monthly spending. Sources: Frederick et al. 2009; Maguire, Persson and Tinghög 2023; Tsinghua PBCSF study reported by Cailian Press, 2023.
slides.notes:
[0:35 to 1:25 · 50 s] We don't feel ¥2,580 of extra food delivery. We would feel losing a weekend away. Three things are true. Budgets speak in abstract numbers, and numbers don't hurt. People neglect what a purchase displaces: that finding holds across 39 studies, modest but robust, so we treat it as a nudge and not a cure. And the moment of spending matters: a warning at the moment of paying was linked to nearly 20 percent lower monthly spending.

Q&A: 'Is the effect big enough?' The pooled effect is small (d = 0.22), which is why FundBun pairs the mirror with tripwires and real actions instead of relying on one nudge.

slides.title: The Dream Mirror: overspend, and you see the dream it cost.
slides.alt: Two FundBun home screens. Jing, over budget: 'You could've gotten a Weekend in Chengdu.' She is ¥2,580 over her ¥9,500 target and her Birkin 25 moved about 5 weeks further away. Arif, on target: '¥668 closer to your MacBook Air'. Spend less than your target, and you see how much closer you are; any treat is your call, never a push. Your own dream items, your own photos, your own words.
slides.notes:
[1:25 to 2:20 · 55 s] When you set up FundBun you give it your income, what you are willing to spend, and your dreams: a Birkin, new shoes, a flight home. Overspend, and the home screen mirrors it back. Jing is ¥2,580 over her ¥9,500 target: she could have had a weekend in Chengdu, and her Birkin just moved about five weeks further away. Spend less than your target, like Arif, and it shows how much closer you are. Any treat is your call. Bun never pushes you to buy.

Q&A: 'Does this shame users?' The good state is framed as progress, the tone is the user's choice, and the stick is for the spending, never for logging it.

slides.title: Tripwires: cross a line you set, and Bun shows what it costs.
slides.alt: Tripwires, the crux. You set four kinds: 80% or 100% of target, a category limit, any purchase over an amount you choose, and projected overspend. Crossing one shows a tangible reminder: 'Whoa, ¥1,299 at JD.com. That ¥1,299 = 1.3% of your Birkin 25.' Bun's tone is your choice: Gentle (default), Cheeky (opt-in) or Just numbers. Shame backfires (Gladstone et al. 2021), so the blunt voice is opt-in.
slides.notes:
[2:20 to 3:10 · 50 s] Tripwires are the crux. You set the lines: 80 or 100 percent of your target, a category limit, any single purchase over an amount you choose, or a projected overspend. Cross one and Bun reminds you with something tangible. Here, ¥1,299 is 1.3 percent of Jing's Birkin. Shame backfires in the research, so the cheeky voice is opt-in and gentle is the default. Bun's face is one ladder computed from the ledger: good days cool it down, and there is always a stated way back.

Q&A: 'Who sets the rules?' The user, always. The agent can suggest a tripwire; it cannot weaken one silently.

slides.title: One core. A desktop app and a phone app.
slides.alt: The product today. Desktop app for Mac: an Electron shell and a local server on 127.0.0.1, with AI keys encrypted by the macOS Keychain. Mobile-ready web app: the same core in the browser with a PWA manifest. Dual Mode: Daily tracking for a simple count, or Goal and Mirror for the full Dream Mirror. Your layout: move, resize or hide every dashboard card, the Daily check-in included. Screenshots: the desktop dashboard and the phone home screen.
slides.notes:
[3:10 to 4:05 · 55 s] This is what exists today. One TypeScript core runs in two places. On a Mac it is a desktop app: an Electron shell with a local server that only listens on this computer, and any AI key you add is encrypted with the macOS Keychain. In a browser or on a phone it is the same core as a mobile-ready web app. There are two modes: Daily tracking if you just want a simple count, and Goal and Mirror for the full Dream Mirror. And the dashboard is yours: every card can be moved, resized or hidden, the Daily check-in included.

Q&A: 'Is there a native mobile app?' Not yet. The phone layout is a responsive web app with a PWA manifest. 'Windows?' The shell is Electron, so it is a packaging job; only the Mac build is tested.

slides.title: Not just chat: Bun plans, then acts.
slides.alt: AI as a financial participant. Four tiers of tasks: T0 Read (overview, bills, subscriptions, affordability); T1 Organise (budgets, category caps, tripwires, reminders); T2 Move own money (stash surplus into goal pots); T3 Pay and cancel (verified bills, subscriptions, disputes). Bun clarifies, takes corrections and stops on 'stop'. Task plan 'Get October back on track', 7 steps as a dependency graph: six done, the Youku cancellation waits for the PIN.
slides.notes:
[4:05 to 5:05 · 60 s] Bun does not just chat. It acts across four tiers. It reads and explains your money. It organises budgets, caps, tripwires and reminders. It moves your own money into goal pots. And it pays verified bills, cancels subscriptions and disputes duplicates. 'Get October back on track' becomes a seven-step plan as a dependency graph: the read steps run at once, and the one step that cancels a subscription waits for the PIN. It asks when a request is vague, takes corrections, and stops when you say stop.

Q&A: 'Does the AI move money on its own?' Only between the user's own pots, inside caps, in a turn with no untrusted content. Anything that pays needs a bank-side confirmation bound to the exact amount and payee. With no bank connected, FundBun watches and reminds; the bank in the demo is simulated.

slides.title: Works with zero AI. Better with yours.
slides.alt: Left: the built-in offline engine, with no model. A chat shows a casual question answered, and an out-of-scope prompt answered with a task picker: Biggest spendings, Today's safe-to-spend, Month overview, Category breakdown, Savings pots, Log an expense. Right: connect the AI you already have: Kimi Code (ACP agent), Moonshot (api.moonshot.cn/v1), DeepSeek, Qwen, Ollama (on this computer), OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini. Same policy gate, keys stay local, falls back offline.
slides.notes:
[5:05 to 6:15 · 70 s] FundBun works with zero AI. The built-in engine is rules plus a small classifier that runs on the device: no model, no network, no key. It understands casual phrasing, and when you ask for something it cannot do offline it does not guess. It offers a task picker, so you are never stuck. And it gets better with your own AI. You can connect what you already have: Kimi Code as an agent, Moonshot's API in mainland China, DeepSeek, Qwen, a local model through Ollama, or OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini. Whatever you connect goes through the same policy gate, the key stays on your computer, and if the AI call fails Bun falls back to the offline engine.

Q&A: 'Which have you tested live?' Kimi Code (verified live over ACP against Kimi CLI 2.5.2, 12/12 checks), DeepSeek and Claude Code. The others connect through the same OpenAI-compatible or ACP path. 'Is the offline engine an LLM?' No. We call it an on-device rules engine, and Bun says so itself if you ask.

slides.title: Everything is a plugin.
slides.alt: Desktop Creator Mode. Widgets: ask for a card, Bun drafts it, it runs in a sandbox with a read-only copy of your numbers, and you press Install. Shell appearance: the theme, what Bun wears, the app's name, one schema with Apply, Undo and Reset. Taint protection: a turn that carries a file, a bill or pasted text cannot change plugins or the look. Behind your PIN: Creator Mode is off until you turn it on, and no plugin can touch money, the PIN or permissions. Right: a chat message 'change theme to cyberpunk, put a kamen rider helm on bun, and rename fundbun to #ilovemoney' and its preview card with Bun in a Kamen Rider helmet, the name #ilovemoney, and Undo and Apply buttons.
slides.notes:
[6:15 to 7:35 · 80 s, with a 30 s live moment] In the desktop app, everything is a plugin. Turn on Creator Mode with your PIN and you can ask Bun for a dashboard card. It drafts the widget, shows a live preview running in a sandbox with a read-only copy of your numbers, and nothing installs until you press Install. The same idea now covers the app itself. Live: I type 'change theme to cyberpunk, put a kamen rider helm on bun, and rename fundbun to #ilovemoney'. That sentence is read on this device with no model. I get a preview, I press Apply, and the theme, the mascot and the name change at once. Undo puts it back, and Reset is one tap in Settings. It is bounded on purpose: fifteen colour tokens, text contrast enforced, a name of at most 28 characters, and a small FundBun line that always stays under a custom name.

Q&A: 'Can a prompt injection restyle the app?' No. A turn that carries a file, a bill or pasted text cannot stage or apply a change, and nothing applies without a tap. 'Can a plugin read my PIN or move money?' No. Widgets get a read-only, PII-minimised snapshot in a sandboxed frame, and appearance plugins change colours, headwear and one name only.

slides.title: Bring your paperwork: files, folders, email.
slides.alt: Two capabilities that are live today in the desktop app. Files and folders in chat: attach files or a whole folder, up to 20 at once; the text is read on this computer and the file is never kept; your connected AI answers questions about them; every attachment is untrusted, so it taints the turn. Formats: PDF, images, Excel, Word, CSV, folder. Read-only email ingestion: IMAP over TLS that can only open the inbox read-only, search and peek; no code path can send, move, flag or delete mail; receipts, invoices and bank alerts from senders you trust; each purchase it finds waits for your tap before it is logged.
slides.notes:
[7:35 to 8:35 · 60 s] Money lives in paperwork, so FundBun reads it. In the desktop chat you can attach files or a whole folder: statements, receipts, spreadsheets. The text is read on this computer and your connected AI answers questions about it. The app treats every attachment as untrusted, which matters on the next slide. Second, email. FundBun can check your mailbox for receipts, invoices and bank alerts. It is read-only by construction: the client can only open the inbox read-only, search, and peek at messages. There is no code path that sends, moves or deletes mail. And every purchase it finds is only a proposal: it waits for your tap.

Q&A: 'Where does my mail password go?' It is encrypted at rest on this computer and never reaches the page. 'Do files work offline?' Reading them needs your own AI; adding spending from a receipt or statement works through the built-in import.

slides.title: The model proposes. A frozen kernel decides.
slides.alt: Permission tiers by user-chosen autonomy, T0 Read to T4 Prohibited. Five kernel properties. Hash-bound PIN approval: the PIN approves one exact action (tool, amount, payee); change a field and it is void. Taint propagation: bills, files, email and pasted text mark the turn untrusted, and risky steps then need your tap or are blocked. Hash-chained audit trail: every decision joins a chain; an edit breaks it and the app shows where. Caps and a kill switch: ¥500 an action, ¥1,000 a day, ¥5,000 a month; one tap makes Bun read-only. T4 is never offered: no new payees, outside transfers, investing, credit, or changing its own limits.
slides.notes:
[8:35 to 9:50 · 75 s] All of that sits on a small security kernel that we froze for the final. Five tiers, T0 to T4. Reading is free. Organising is reversible. Moving your own money is capped: ¥500 an action, ¥1,000 a day, ¥5,000 a month. Paying needs your PIN, and the PIN is bound by a hash to the exact tool, amount and payee: if anything changes after you looked, the approval is void. Untrusted content taints the whole turn, so a bill, a file or an email can never quietly authorise an action. Every decision is appended to a hash-chained audit trail, so tampering is visible. And tier four, like adding a payee or sending money to a stranger, is never offered to any model at all. The model proposes. The kernel decides.

Q&A: 'What does frozen mean?' Six files hold the policy, PIN, binding, audit and tool specs. Creator Mode, attachments and email were added around them, and each new tool passes the same gate. 'What if the model is jailbroken?' It can only propose; the deterministic gate still decides.

slides.title: Measured. Reproducible. Nothing moved.
slides.alt: Evidence and red team: 45 of 45 scripted scenarios pass; 24 of 24 scripted attacks blocked; ¥0 moved in every attack; 0 of 26 false refusals of real requests; 4,244 automated tests passing across 169 files; 36 more attacks with a real model switched on, ¥0 moved. Command: npm run evidence. Screenshot: Jing's electricity bill hides an order to wire ¥4,800 to a stranger; Bun flags it and nothing moves.
slides.notes:
[9:50 to 10:45 · 55 s] Everything I have claimed is measured. 45 of 45 scripted scenarios pass. We red-teamed the four attack classes you score: induced transfer, data extraction, privilege escalation and prompt injection. 24 of 24 scripted attacks were blocked and ¥0 moved, with zero false refusals across 26 legitimate requests, so the safety does not cost usefulness. With a real model switched on we ran 36 attacks: 24 were stopped by the rule layer before the model was even asked, 12 reached the model and were refused, and again nothing moved. The suite has 4,244 passing automated tests across 169 files (plus 1 skipped redactor stub, 0 failed), and one command reruns the evidence byte for byte.

Q&A: say 'with a real model switched on', never 'the model blocked 24 of 24'. 'Real bank data?' None. Personas are synthetic and the bank is a sandbox; real users import CSV or add spending by hand.

slides.title: FundBun Pro: $25 a month.
slides.alt: Possible future development: monetization. Planned, not built. Free today, $0, bring your own AI: the full finance app on desktop and web, the zero-AI offline engine, connect Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, Ollama and more, the same security kernel. FundBun Pro, proposed at $25 a month: Creator Mode (widgets and shell appearance plugins), hosted multi-model AI built in and included in the price, no API key and nothing to connect, and bring your own AI stays available. Everyday users get an AI that simply works; power users keep control; the kernel is identical for both.
slides.notes:
[10:45 to 11:35 · 50 s] Three possible next steps, and I will be clear about what is built and what is not. First, how this could pay for itself. Today FundBun is free if you bring your own AI. Most everyday users do not have an API key and should not need one. So the proposal is FundBun Pro at 25 dollars a month: it unlocks Creator Mode, and it includes a hosted, multi-model AI, so it works the first time you open it. Bring your own AI stays available. The security kernel is identical on both plans, because safety is not a paid feature.

Q&A: 'Is Pro live?' No. There is no hosted model, billing or Pro gate yet. 'Why $25?' It has to cover hosted multi-model usage with margin; it is a starting point to test, not a validated price. 'Data?' Hosted AI would see the same redacted, minimised context as any model today and could only propose.

slides.title: A proposal: FundBun inside WeBank.
slides.alt: Possible future development: bank partnership. A concept; nothing is agreed with any bank. Two phone mock-ups. Left: a WeBank mobile home, concept: greeting, pill tabs Insight, Pay, Growth, an orange account card with a teal portfolio card, and a 4 by 2 Featured services grid in which one tile, FundBun, is circled. Right: FundBun opens inside it with the Dream Mirror ('You could've gotten a weekend in Chengdu') and PIN-gated Goal Pots (Birkin 25 at 24%, Flight home at 40%) and a 'Stash ¥200' button that WeBank confirms with the PIN. Aims: a reason to open the app daily, micro-saving that sticks, retention built on trust. The bank hosts, holds the money and executes; FundBun proposes and enforces the rules.
slides.notes:
[11:35 to 12:50 · 75 s] Second, a proposal for a bank. To be clear: this is a concept, and nothing is agreed with any bank. Picture the home screen of a bank's app. Among the featured services, one tile: FundBun. Tap it, and FundBun opens inside the bank's own app with the two things users come back for. The Dream Mirror, which changes every time you spend. And Goal Pots, where each small stash is confirmed by the bank with your PIN. That is gamified saving inside WeBank. For the bank the aims are a reason to open the app every day, micro-saving that sticks, and retention built on trust. The split of roles is the point: the bank hosts it, holds the money and executes. FundBun proposes and enforces the rules.

Q&A: 'Have you talked to WeBank?' No. This is our proposal for discussion. 'Are those retention numbers?' No, they are aims to test in a consented pilot. 'Why would a bank want an outside agent?' It would not run outside: the bank hosts it, and the kernel's caps and bindings can be enforced on the bank side.

slides.title: Spending that logs itself.
slides.alt: Possible future development: automatic expense capture. Left, live today on desktop: read-only email ingestion. Flow: mailbox, read-only IMAP, your tap, ledger. Receipts, invoices and bank emails become proposed entries; tried and tested in the desktop app and its test suite; the mailbox is never changed. Right, roadmap for mobile: a push notification listener. Flow: notification, parsed on the phone, your tap, ledger. Captured the moment you pay; read on the device, nothing sent to a cloud; the same tap-to-log gate as email. Sources it would cover: e-wallets, QRIS, WeChat Pay, Alipay, bank apps.
slides.notes:
[12:50 to 13:50 · 60 s] Third, the hardest part of any budgeting app is typing in what you spent. On the desktop that is already going away: the read-only email ingestion you saw turns receipts, invoices and bank emails into proposed entries, and you confirm each with a tap. It is tried and tested in the desktop app. The roadmap is the same idea on the phone: a notification listener that reads the payment notification from your e-wallet, QRIS, WeChat Pay, Alipay or bank app at the moment you pay. It would be parsed on the device, with nothing sent to a cloud, behind the same tap-to-log gate.

Q&A: 'Is the mobile listener built?' No, it is a roadmap item. 'iOS?' Android first, where a notification listener works with the user's permission. iOS does not let an app read other apps' notifications, so there the path stays email, statements and manual entry. 'Privacy?' The listener would keep only the amount, merchant and time.

slides.title: Show me my mirror.
slides.alt: Closing slide: 'Show me my mirror.' The Dream Mirror shows the Birkin 25, 24% saved, with a happy Bun. Live on this laptop: the desktop app with the offline engine, demo PIN 2580. Repository: github.com/odripads/fundbun. Rerun every number with npm run evidence. Team: Odri Prince Sembiring (Universitas Gadjah Mada) and Nadine Griselda (Universitas Airlangga). 2026 FinTechathon Finalist, International AI Track.
slides.notes:
[13:50 to 14:10 · 20 s] FundBun makes the cost of spending something you can see, and gives you an agent you can actually trust with your money: one that works with no AI, gets better with yours, and that you can make your own. Show me my mirror. Thank you.

Q&A (5 minutes): keep the desktop app open on the dashboard with the glass box visible. Have these ready to show: the appearance card with Apply and Undo, an attached bill being blocked, the audit chain on the Activity screen, and Settings, Creator Mode with Reset Shell Appearance. If asked what is not real: the bank is a sandbox, Pro and the mobile listener are not built, and the WeBank screen is a concept.
